reference: Independent shell assertions, a fixed Python-authored USTAR FIFO/member archive, and GNU tar decoding of pax output. No external GNU pax CLI parity is claimed.
coverage: Shared engine writer hardlinks/FIFOs and repeated archive context reset.
Independent FIFO extraction with original modes and restored umask.
G28: POSIX grouped option letters (-wf, -rf, -rvf), attached option-arguments, -x ustar|pax, -b, and -r -p o owner restoration.
exclusions: Character/block devices, copy mode, unsafe paths and concurrency are not exercised.

Distinct source inodes mapped onto one archive pathname can make a later hardlink alias bind to the replacement data, as independently observed with GNU tar. General preservation of source data/topology across conflicting archive member names is not claimed.

cases.purpose: Pax creation emits regular hardlinks and FIFO metadata readable by GNU tar; a later archive containing only an alias has its own fresh context.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/mkdir restored one-member
printf shared > original
/usr/bin/ln original twin
/usr/bin/mkfifo -m 0640 pipe
pax -w -f archive.tar original twin pipe
/usr/bin/tar -xf archive.tar -C restored
[[ restored/original -ef restored/twin && -p restored/pipe && $(<restored/original) == shared ]]
pax -w -f next.tar twin
/usr/bin/tar -xf next.tar -C one-member
[[ $(<one-member/twin) == shared ]]
printf 'pax writer links fifo and context verified\n'
cases.stdout: pax writer links fifo and context verified

cases.purpose: The shared pax reader extracts fixed independent FIFO metadata without opening a stream and preserves its normal pax mode contract despite umask077.
cases.script:
printf '%s' '' | /usr/bin/base64 -d > oracle.tar
/usr/bin/mkdir restored
umask 077
(cd restored; pax -r -f ../oracle.tar)
[[ -p restored/pipe && $(<restored/after) == 'fifo sibling' ]]
/usr/bin/stat -c %a restored/pipe restored/after
: > after-mask
/usr/bin/stat -c %a after-mask

cases.purpose: -o uid:=, gid:=, uname:=, gname:= store the given owner in the ustar header (tar --owner/--group).
cases.script:
field() { dd if="$1" bs=1 skip=$(( $2 * 512 + $3 )) count=$4 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\0'; echo; }
printf x > f
pax -w -o uid:=0 -o gid:=7 -o uname:=root -o gname:=lp -f a.tar f
field a.tar 0 108 7; field a.tar 0 116 7; field a.tar 0 265 32; field a.tar 0 297 32

cases.purpose: -o exclude:=PATTERN skips members anywhere in the tree, -o sort:=name orders directory entries, and -a appends before the end-of-archive blocks.
cases.script:
mkdir -p s/d
printf a > s/b; printf o > s/a.o; printf f > s/d/f; printf c > s/c
pax -w -o sort:=name -o exclude:='*.o' -o exclude:=d -f x.tar s
pax -f x.tar
printf n > new
pax -w -a -f x.tar new
pax -f x.tar | tail -2
pax -w -a -f fresh.tar new && pax -f fresh.tar
cases.stdout:
s
s/b
s/c
s/c
new
new

cases.purpose: G28: POSIX utility syntax groups option letters, so pax -wf ARCHIVE FILE writes and pax -rf ARCHIVE reads (GNU tar decodes the result); -fARCHIVE takes an attached argument.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/mkdir s o
printf hi > s/f
pax -wf a.pax s </dev/null
/usr/bin/tar -tf a.pax
(cd o && pax -rf ../a.pax </dev/null)
/usr/bin/cat o/s/f; echo
pax -fa.pax
pax -wdf d.pax s && pax -f d.pax
cases.stdout:
s
s/f
hi
s
s/f
s

cases.purpose: G28: -x ustar (and -x pax, -xustar) names the write format instead of being read as file operands; an unsupported format is a usage error.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/mkdir s
printf hi > s/f
pax -w -x ustar -f u.tar s
/usr/bin/tar -tf u.tar
pax -w -xpax -b 10240 -f p.tar s && pax -f p.tar
pax -w -x cpio -f c.tar s 2>/tmp/err || echo rc=$?
[[ -e c.tar ]] || echo no-archive
/usr/bin/grep -c cpio /tmp/err
cases.stdout:
s
s/f
s
s/f
rc=2
no-archive
1

cases.purpose: H2: pax -r -p o (and -p e) chowns members to the archived owner; for a foreign uid as non-root that reports the failure (file before its directory). Plain -r does not chown.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/mkdir s a b
printf hi > s/f
/usr/bin/tar --owner=12345 --group=12345 -cf o.tar s
(cd a && pax -r -p o -f ../o.tar) 2>/tmp/err || echo rc=$?
/usr/bin/sed 's/^.*pax: /pax: /' /tmp/err
(cd b && pax -rf ../o.tar) && echo plain-ok
pax -r -p z -f o.tar 2>/dev/null || echo rc=$?
cases.stdout:
rc=1
pax: s/f: Cannot change ownership to uid 12345, gid 12345: Invalid argument
pax: s: Cannot change ownership to uid 12345, gid 12345: Invalid argument
plain-ok
rc=2
